v1.text: A 68 year old man with an intrathecal morphine pump treating post-amputation pain is admitted for pump failure. The intrathecal pump is programmed to administer {{dose}} mg of morphine daily. Convert the intrathecal morphine dose to an intravenous equivalent.

v2.text: A 53 year old woman with metastatic pancreatic cancer sustained a traumatic fracture of her right humerus. Prior to the injury, she was taking hydromorphone every 6 hours for a total administration of {{oral}} mg/day. She underwent ORIF of her right humerus, and by postoperative day 2, she was taking hydromorphone {{oral_dose}} mg PO every 4 hours and additional hydromorphone {{iv_dose}} mg IV every 4 hours. Convert her total current hydromorphone administration as of postoperative day 2 to entirely PO dosing in order to begin an opioid taper plan.

v3.text: A 9 year old child with 30% body surface area burns has been receiving hydromorphone via a PCA pump. The patient used {{dose_4hr}} mg of intravenous hydromorphone over the past 4 hours. The primary burn service would like to switch the patient to oral morphine. Convert the hydromorphone usage into oral morphine in mg/4hr.
